title: fix: scheduled conversation reviews report delivery failure
body: Fixes #188131 ## What Problem This Solves A scheduled review can finish inside its existing Control UI conversation, save its work, and display the answer, while the automation still reports failed completion and “Not delivered.” This happens when announce delivery has no external messaging route: the shared-session runner treats missing channel coordinates as a delivery failure even after the existing conversation writer commits the answer. ## User Impact A persistent same-conversation announcement now records successful delivery when its settled answer is actually committed to that destination. Users can rely on the completion state without configuring an unrelated messaging channel or sending the review elsewhere. The answer remains a single conversation result; this does not fabricate a transport or message-tool send. Explicit external destinations, remembered external routes, unavailable creating conversations, and different source/execution destinations remain outside the internal fallback. Native-only payloads that cannot produce a conversation entry remain undelivered. Supported main-session aliases use the existing Cron key resolver. Quiet runs, deliberate silence, cancellation, and current session/operator authority retain their existing owners and behavior. There is no configuration, schema, or public protocol change. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing session-event settlement path already owns the useful conversation write. It now preserves the writer’s committed-versus-skipped result and returns the fact that a write committed, which the scheduled runner consumes only when the internal destination is the same session. The runner rechecks the current delivery route before that commit and preserves its existing occurrence and authority fences. This keeps result persistence and delivery policy with their current owners. It avoids another dispatcher, duplicate result writes, error-text matching, or treating successful computation alone as delivery evidence. The focused regression extends the existing integration fixture, with a small test-line allocation for internal delivery, deliberate silence, and a genuinely unavailable external destination. ## Evidence On base 87facf07d6b4907846c4a8e4c7ae551f85571420, a normal administrator asked for one later review in the same conversation, then changed a criterion before execution. The single scheduled run produced a useful visible review and a 19,034-byte saved file; all three original files kept their hashes. Its native event and run receipt nevertheless reported `status: ok`, `completionStatus: failed`, and `deliveryStatus: not-delivered` with the missing-channel error. The new real-owner integration case failed on unchanged production code after confirming one persisted result, with `delivered: false` instead of `true`; the six existing cases passed. The current candidate passes all 14 cases, including internal silence, explicit external failure, native-only output, configured main keys, legacy agent-main aliases, global-scope main aliases, and a different-conversation control. Only model decisions and the external channel transport are synthetic in that fixture; scheduling, admission, conversation persistence, and settlement use their production owners. Remote validation passed changed-file formatting/lint and all selected production/test compiler graphs on the final tree. The initial 754 tests across 53 affected files passed; after the reviewed receipt/key corrections, all 268 tests in 13 affected files passed. The final global-main comparison correction also passes all 163 tests in eight affected files, retaining applicable earlier results. The two correction batches took 278.89 and 194.28 seconds. The 13-case predecessor fixture measured 49.91 seconds in its focused run because it exercises the actual Gateway, session admission, SQLite result commit, and settlement together. Broad hosted checks and the final independent recheck are clean on e537ad08b4612ce28ec907e8cf4cec76ac1eea9c. The corrected live run accepted a new criterion on the same job before execution and produced a 20,930-byte review using the amended 60-book capacity and 100-book overflow. All original files and the earlier review kept their hashes. One native execution settled as `completionStatus: succeeded`, `delivered: true`, and `deliveryStatus: delivered`, with the internal fallback recorded and no delivery error. The conversation displayed one useful final result, unchanged after reload. The successful one-shot removed itself normally. The captures compare failed-job history before the fix with global history afterward because the successful job has already retired. The 43-second recording joins the actual scheduling/criterion and completion/reload windows; idle time and observer recovery are omitted, and no model work was replayed. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![A useful scheduled review with failed completion and Not delivered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/557a9956-6d87-4025-b78a-c17037518128) | ![The new review is Delivered and uses the amended 60\-book capacity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b820e34b-cd50-419e-8f92-8a7f6daa525d) | ### Condensed scheduling, criterion update, successful history and conversation reload https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd0845bd-05b5-4ad3-bda7-f096cfdb5469 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 87facf07d6b4907846c4a8e4c7ae551f85571420 - Exact head: `e537ad08b4612ce28ec907e8cf4cec76ac1eea9c` - Scenario: Ask for one later review in the same conversation, amend a capacity criterion before execution, then inspect its useful saved result and native delivery/completion\. No external messaging route is configured\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.9; Gateway build 2026\.10\.9\-e537ad08b461\-2026\-10\-30T07\-44\-08\.147Z; fresh UI document 2026\.10\.9\-e537ad08b461 - Native completion: failed → succeeded - Native delivery: not\-delivered → delivered; internal fallback confirmed - Execution and persistence: One scheduled run; one visible result, unchanged after reload - Saved work: 20,930\-byte new review; original packet and prior review unchanged - Exact final Gateway and fresh document identities verified independently\. - The amended criterion was accepted on the same job before execution; the result correctly uses 60 spaces and 100 books of overflow\. - Before uses retained failed\-job history; after uses global history because the successful one\-shot removes itself\. This lifecycle difference does not change the accounting comparison\. - Both runs use the same conversation, packet, viewport and theme; the new 60\-book criterion deliberately differs from the earlier 72\-book criterion to prove the fresh amendment was used\. - Runtime identity details are redacted\. The recording joins two actual capture windows; idle time and observer recovery are omitted and no model work was replayed\.
